_doc: Kho điểm ngữ pháp tiếng Tây Ban Nha (es-419 trung tính) của LexKite. 100% tự soạn: tên điểm, câu "Can …" và ví dụ là của LexKite, không chép Plan Curricular del Instituto Cervantes hay sách giáo trình (CONTENT-RULES §1). lessons = id bài es (chưa có → []); tenses = khóa của scripts/target/conjugate.mjs; kiểm: node scripts/content-qa/grammar-map-check.mjs --tl es; id điểm KHÔNG đổi/tái dùng.

points.name: ser: identity, origin, profession
points.can_do_en: Can use ser to say who someone is, where they are from and what they do.
points.example: Soy Ana y soy de México. Mi papá es ingeniero.
points.example_en: I'm Ana and I'm from Mexico. My dad is an engineer.

points.name: estar: location
points.can_do_en: Can use estar to say where a person, place or thing is.
points.example: Mi casa está cerca del parque.
points.example_en: My house is near the park.

points.name: estar: states and feelings
points.can_do_en: Can use estar to describe how someone feels or what state they are in today.
points.example: Hoy estoy cansado, pero estoy contento.
points.example_en: Today I'm tired, but I'm happy.

points.name: ser vs estar (first contrast)
points.can_do_en: Can tell apart lasting traits with ser and temporary states with estar in simple sentences.
points.example: Mi hermano es alto, pero hoy está enfermo.
points.example_en: My brother is tall, but today he is sick.

points.name: hay: there is / there are
points.can_do_en: Can use hay to say what exists in a place.
points.example: Hay un banco en la esquina y hay dos tiendas.
points.example_en: There is a bank on the corner and there are two shops.

points.name: present tense of -ar verbs
points.can_do_en: Can conjugate regular -ar verbs in the present to talk about what I do.
points.example: Hablo español y trabajo en una tienda.
points.example_en: I speak Spanish and I work in a shop.

points.name: present tense of -er and -ir verbs
points.can_do_en: Can conjugate regular -er and -ir verbs in the present for everyday actions.
points.example: Como pan y escribo una carta.
points.example_en: I eat bread and write a letter.

points.name: present: irregular yo forms
points.can_do_en: Can use common verbs with an irregular yo form such as hacer, salir, poner and traer.
points.example: Hago la tarea y salgo a las ocho.
points.example_en: I do my homework and leave at eight.

points.name: tener: age and possession
points.can_do_en: Can use tener to say my age, my family and what I have.
points.example: Tengo veinte años y dos hermanos.
points.example_en: I'm twenty years old and I have two brothers.

points.name: ir a + place
points.can_do_en: Can use ir with a to say where I am going.
points.example: Voy al mercado con mi mamá.
points.example_en: I go to the market with my mom.

points.name: stem changes e to ie
points.can_do_en: Can use common verbs that change e to ie in the present, such as querer and empezar.
points.example: Quiero un café y empiezo a las nueve.
points.example_en: I want a coffee and I start at nine.

points.name: stem changes o to ue
points.can_do_en: Can use common verbs that change o to ue in the present, such as poder and dormir.
points.example: Duermo ocho horas y puedo estudiar por la tarde.
points.example_en: I sleep eight hours and I can study in the afternoon.

points.name: reflexive verbs for daily routine
points.can_do_en: Can use reflexive verbs to describe my morning and evening routine.
points.example: Me levanto a las seis y me ducho.
points.example_en: I get up at six and take a shower.

points.name: gustar: likes and dislikes
points.can_do_en: Can say what I like with gustar, choosing gusta or gustan by the thing liked.
points.example: Me gusta el chocolate y me gustan los gatos.
points.example_en: I like chocolate and I like cats.

points.name: gender of nouns
points.can_do_en: Can match masculine and feminine nouns with the right article and adjective.
points.example: El libro es rojo y la mesa es blanca.
points.example_en: The book is red and the table is white.

points.name: plural of nouns
points.can_do_en: Can form plurals with -s, -es and the z to c change.
points.example: Tengo dos lápices y tres libros.
points.example_en: I have two pencils and three books.

points.name: definite articles el, la, los, las
points.can_do_en: Can use el, la, los and las with nouns I already know about.
points.example: La niña tiene el balón.
points.example_en: The girl has the ball.

points.name: indefinite articles un, una, unos, unas
points.can_do_en: Can use un, una, unos and unas to introduce something new.
points.example: Tengo un perro y una gata.
points.example_en: I have a dog and a cat.

points.name: adjective agreement
points.can_do_en: Can make adjectives agree in gender and number with the noun.
points.example: Las casas pequeñas son bonitas.
points.example_en: The small houses are pretty.

points.name: possessives mi, tu, su, nuestro
points.can_do_en: Can use short possessives to say whose people and things they are.
points.example: Mi hermana y tu hermano son amigos.
points.example_en: My sister and your brother are friends.

points.name: demonstratives este, ese, aquel
points.can_do_en: Can point to things near and far with este, ese and aquel.
points.example: Esta casa es grande y aquel parque es bonito.
points.example_en: This house is big and that park over there is pretty.

points.name: subject pronouns
points.can_do_en: Can use yo, tú, él, ella, usted and ellos when the subject needs to be clear.
points.example: Yo trabajo y ella estudia.
points.example_en: I work and she studies.

points.name: question words
points.can_do_en: Can ask simple questions with qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cómo and cuántos.
points.example: ¿Dónde vives? ¿Cuántos años tienes?
points.example_en: Where do you live? How old are you?

points.name: yes/no questions
points.can_do_en: Can ask yes/no questions by rising intonation and answer with sí or no.
points.example: ¿Hablas inglés? Sí, un poco.
points.example_en: Do you speak English? Yes, a little.

points.name: basic negation with no
points.can_do_en: Can make a sentence negative by putting no before the verb.
points.example: No tengo hermanos. No me gusta el café.
points.example_en: I don't have siblings. I don't like coffee.

points.name: prepositions a, de, en
points.can_do_en: Can use a, de and en for direction, origin and place.
points.example: Vivo en Lima y trabajo en el centro.
points.example_en: I live in Lima and I work downtown.

points.name: contractions al and del
points.can_do_en: Can use al and del instead of a el and de el.
points.example: Voy al cine después del trabajo.
points.example_en: I go to the movies after work.

points.name: numbers 0 to 100
points.can_do_en: Can say and understand numbers from zero to one hundred.
points.example: Tengo treinta y cinco años.
points.example_en: I'm thirty-five years old.

points.name: telling the time
points.can_do_en: Can tell the time using es la and son las.
points.example: Son las tres y media. Es la una.
points.example_en: It's half past three. It's one o'clock.

points.name: days, months and dates
points.can_do_en: Can say the days, the months and simple dates.
points.example: Mi cumpleaños es el cinco de mayo.
points.example_en: My birthday is on the fifth of May.

points.name: weather with hacer and llover
points.can_do_en: Can describe the weather with hacer, hay and llover.
points.example: Hoy hace frío y llueve.
points.example_en: Today it's cold and it's raining.

points.name: muy and mucho
points.can_do_en: Can choose muy before adjectives and adverbs, and mucho after verbs.
points.example: Como mucho pan y es muy rico.
points.example_en: I eat a lot of bread and it's very tasty.

points.name: también and tampoco
points.can_do_en: Can agree with a positive statement using también and with a negative one using tampoco.
points.example: Yo también trabajo. Ella tampoco come carne.
points.example_en: I work too. She doesn't eat meat either.

points.name: tú and usted
points.can_do_en: Can choose usted for polite or formal speech and tú for friends and family.
points.example: ¿Cómo está usted, señora López?
points.example_en: How are you, Mrs. López?

points.name: y, pero, porque, o
points.can_do_en: Can link short ideas with y, pero, porque and o.
points.example: Estudio español porque me gusta, pero es difícil.
points.example_en: I study Spanish because I like it, but it's hard.

points.name: ir a + infinitive (first use)
points.can_do_en: Can say what I am going to do soon with ir a and an infinitive.
points.example: Esta tarde voy a comer con mi tía.
points.example_en: This afternoon I'm going to have lunch with my aunt.

points.name: preterite of regular verbs
points.can_do_en: Can talk about finished past actions with regular preterite forms.
points.example: Ayer comí tacos y hablé con Luis.
points.example_en: Yesterday I ate tacos and talked with Luis.

points.name: preterite of ser and ir
points.can_do_en: Can use fui, fuiste, fue and the other forms of ser and ir in the past.
points.example: Fui al cine y la película fue buena.
points.example_en: I went to the movies and the film was good.

points.name: common irregular preterites
points.can_do_en: Can use common irregular preterites such as hacer, tener, estar, poder and decir.
points.example: Hice la cena y tuve una llamada importante.
points.example_en: I made dinner and had an important call.

points.name: preterite stem changes (e to i, o to u)
points.can_do_en: Can use the stem-changing preterite of -ir verbs in the third person.
points.example: Ella durmió poco y pidió un café.
points.example_en: She slept little and asked for a coffee.

points.name: preterite spelling changes
points.can_do_en: Can write the spelling changes in yo forms such as llegué, busqué and empecé.
points.example: Llegué temprano y busqué la llave.
points.example_en: I arrived early and looked for the key.

points.name: imperfect of regular verbs
points.can_do_en: Can describe habits and scenes in the past with regular imperfect forms.
points.example: De niño jugaba en el parque y comía helado.
points.example_en: As a child I played in the park and ate ice cream.

points.name: imperfect of ser, ir and ver
points.can_do_en: Can use era, iba and veía to describe the past.
points.example: Antes era tímido e íbamos a la playa.
points.example_en: I used to be shy and we went to the beach.

points.name: preterite vs imperfect (first contrast)
points.can_do_en: Can tell a background situation in the imperfect from an event in the preterite.
points.example: Cuando llegué, mi hermana dormía.
points.example_en: When I arrived, my sister was sleeping.

points.name: estar + gerund
points.can_do_en: Can say what is happening right now with estar and a gerund.
points.example: Estoy cocinando y mi hermano está leyendo.
points.example_en: I'm cooking and my brother is reading.

points.name: present perfect (introduction)
points.can_do_en: Can use he, has, ha plus a participle for recent experience and unfinished periods.
points.example: Hoy he comido muy bien. ¿Ya has visto la película?
points.example_en: Today I've eaten very well. Have you seen the movie yet?

points.name: irregular participles
points.can_do_en: Can use irregular participles such as hecho, escrito, dicho, visto and puesto.
points.example: He escrito el correo y he hecho la cena.
points.example_en: I've written the email and I've made dinner.

points.name: affirmative tú imperative
points.can_do_en: Can give simple instructions to a friend with the tú imperative.
points.example: Abre la ventana y ven aquí.
points.example_en: Open the window and come here.

points.name: negative tú imperative
points.can_do_en: Can tell a friend what not to do using no and the subjunctive form.
points.example: No abras la puerta ni hables fuerte.
points.example_en: Don't open the door or talk loudly.

points.name: usted imperative
points.can_do_en: Can politely tell someone to do something using the usted form.
points.example: Pase, por favor, y siéntese.
points.example_en: Come in, please, and have a seat.

points.name: reflexive verbs in more tenses
points.can_do_en: Can use reflexive verbs in the preterite and with a change of meaning.
points.example: Me desperté tarde y me vestí rápido.
points.example_en: I woke up late and got dressed quickly.

points.name: reciprocal actions
points.can_do_en: Can use reflexive pronouns for actions people do to each other.
points.example: Nos vemos los lunes y nos escribimos mucho.
points.example_en: We see each other on Mondays and write to each other a lot.

points.name: gustar-type verbs
points.can_do_en: Can use encantar, interesar, molestar and doler with an indirect object.
points.example: A ella le encantan los museos y le interesa el arte.
points.example_en: She loves museums and is interested in art.

points.name: indirect object pronouns
points.can_do_en: Can use me, te, le, nos and les to say who receives or benefits.
points.example: Le doy un regalo a mi hermano y te escribo mañana.
points.example_en: I give my brother a gift and I'll write to you tomorrow.

points.name: direct object pronouns
points.can_do_en: Can replace a known noun with lo, la, los or las.
points.example: ¿El libro? Lo tengo yo. A Marta la veo mañana.
points.example_en: The book? I have it. I'll see Marta tomorrow.

points.name: pronouns with infinitives and gerunds
points.can_do_en: Can attach pronouns to an infinitive or a gerund, or put them before the conjugated verb.
points.example: Quiero verla y voy a llamarte.
points.example_en: I want to see her and I'm going to call you.

points.name: pronouns after prepositions
points.can_do_en: Can use mí, ti, él, conmigo and contigo after prepositions.
points.example: Este regalo es para ti. ¿Vienes conmigo?
points.example_en: This gift is for you. Are you coming with me?

points.name: personal a
points.can_do_en: Can add a before a direct object that is a specific person.
points.example: Conozco a tu hermano, pero no conozco su casa.
points.example_en: I know your brother, but I don't know his house.

points.name: saber vs conocer
points.can_do_en: Can choose saber for facts and skills and conocer for people and places.
points.example: Sé cocinar, pero no conozco este restaurante.
points.example_en: I know how to cook, but I don't know this restaurant.

points.name: ser vs estar with adjectives
points.can_do_en: Can use ser for what something is like and estar for how it is now.
points.example: La sopa es buena, pero hoy está fría.
points.example_en: The soup is good, but today it's cold.

points.name: tener que and hay que
points.can_do_en: Can express obligation with tener que and general necessity with hay que.
points.example: Tengo que estudiar. Hay que llegar temprano.
points.example_en: I have to study. One must arrive early.

points.name: poder and querer + infinitive
points.can_do_en: Can ask, offer and say what I want with poder, querer and an infinitive.
points.example: ¿Puedes ayudarme? Quiero aprender más.
points.example_en: Can you help me? I want to learn more.

points.name: acabar de + infinitive
points.can_do_en: Can say something has just happened with acabar de.
points.example: Acabo de llegar y todavía no he cenado.
points.example_en: I've just arrived and I haven't had dinner yet.

points.name: por and para (first uses)
points.can_do_en: Can use para for purpose and goal and por for movement through a place.
points.example: Estudio para ser médico y camino por el parque.
points.example_en: I study to become a doctor and I walk through the park.

points.name: más / menos ... que
points.can_do_en: Can compare two things with más que and menos que.
points.example: Mi casa es más grande que la tuya.
points.example_en: My house is bigger than yours.

points.name: superlatives
points.can_do_en: Can say which one is the most or the best with el más and el mejor.
points.example: Es el mejor restaurante de la ciudad.
points.example_en: It's the best restaurant in the city.

points.name: tan / tanto ... como
points.can_do_en: Can say two things are equal with tan, tanto and como.
points.example: Ella es tan alta como yo y tiene tantos libros como tú.
points.example_en: She's as tall as I am and has as many books as you.

points.name: adverbs in -mente
points.can_do_en: Can form adverbs from adjectives with -mente.
points.example: Habla claramente y trabaja rápidamente.
points.example_en: She speaks clearly and works quickly.

points.name: frequency adverbs
points.can_do_en: Can say how often I do things with siempre, a veces and nunca.
points.example: Siempre desayuno temprano y nunca como carne.
points.example_en: I always have breakfast early and I never eat meat.

points.name: ya and todavía
points.can_do_en: Can use ya and todavía to say whether something has happened.
points.example: Ya terminé, pero todavía no he cenado.
points.example_en: I've already finished, but I haven't had dinner yet.

points.name: numbers above 100
points.can_do_en: Can say prices and years using hundreds and thousands.
points.example: Cuesta mil doscientos pesos.
points.example_en: It costs one thousand two hundred pesos.

points.name: ordinal numbers
points.can_do_en: Can use primero to décimo to say floors, order and dates.
points.example: Vivo en el tercer piso.
points.example_en: I live on the third floor.

points.name: prepositions of place
points.can_do_en: Can say where things are with al lado de, enfrente de, entre and cerca de.
points.example: El banco está al lado del parque y enfrente de la escuela.
points.example_en: The bank is next to the park and across from the school.

points.name: hace + time
points.can_do_en: Can say how long ago something happened with hace and a time expression.
points.example: Llegué hace tres días.
points.example_en: I arrived three days ago.

points.name: por qué vs porque
points.can_do_en: Can ask with por qué and answer with porque.
points.example: ¿Por qué estudias español? Porque me encanta.
points.example_en: Why do you study Spanish? Because I love it.

points.name: porque, por eso, así que
points.can_do_en: Can explain a reason and a result in two linked sentences.
points.example: No salí porque llovía; por eso me quedé en casa.
points.example_en: I didn't go out because it was raining, so I stayed home.

points.name: relative clauses with que
points.can_do_en: Can add information about a noun with que.
points.example: El libro que compré es muy bueno.
points.example_en: The book that I bought is very good.

points.name: simple future (regular)
points.can_do_en: Can make predictions and promises with regular future forms.
points.example: Mañana llamaré a mi tía y te escribiré.
points.example_en: Tomorrow I'll call my aunt and write to you.

points.name: irregular future stems
points.can_do_en: Can use irregular future stems such as tendr-, har-, podr- and dir-.
points.example: Tendré tiempo y haré las compras el sábado.
points.example_en: I'll have time and do the shopping on Saturday.

points.name: future for probability
points.can_do_en: Can guess about the present with the future tense.
points.example: Ya serán las diez. Estará en casa.
points.example_en: It must be ten o'clock by now. He must be at home.

points.name: conditional for polite requests
points.can_do_en: Can ask politely with podría, querría and me gustaría.
points.example: ¿Podría abrir la ventana? Me gustaría un té.
points.example_en: Could you open the window? I'd like a tea.

points.name: conditional for advice
points.can_do_en: Can give advice with deberías, yo que tú and the conditional.
points.example: Yo que tú, hablaría con ella. Deberías descansar.
points.example_en: If I were you, I'd talk to her. You should rest.

points.name: past perfect (pluscuamperfecto)
points.can_do_en: Can show that one past event happened before another.
points.example: Cuando llegamos, la película ya había empezado.
points.example_en: When we arrived, the movie had already started.

points.name: preterite vs imperfect in stories
points.can_do_en: Can tell a story with the imperfect for scene and the preterite for events.
points.example: Era de noche y llovía cuando sonó el teléfono.
points.example_en: It was night and it was raining when the phone rang.

points.name: verbs that change meaning in the preterite
points.can_do_en: Can use saber, conocer, querer and poder with a different meaning in the preterite.
points.example: Ayer supe la verdad. Conocí a su hermano en la fiesta.
points.example_en: Yesterday I found out the truth. I met her brother at the party.

points.name: present perfect vs preterite
points.can_do_en: Can choose the perfect for a period still open and the preterite for a closed one.
points.example: Este año he viajado mucho, pero el año pasado viajé poco.
points.example_en: This year I've traveled a lot, but last year I traveled little.

points.name: estar in the imperfect + gerund
points.can_do_en: Can describe an action in progress in the past with estaba and a gerund.
points.example: Estaba cocinando cuando llegaste.
points.example_en: I was cooking when you arrived.

points.name: present subjunctive forms
points.can_do_en: Can form the present subjunctive of regular and stem-changing verbs.
points.example: Espero que tengas un buen viaje.
points.example_en: I hope you have a good trip.

points.name: subjunctive after wishes and requests
points.can_do_en: Can say what I want others to do with querer que and the subjunctive.
points.example: Quiero que vengas a mi fiesta.
points.example_en: I want you to come to my party.

points.name: subjunctive after emotions
points.can_do_en: Can react to a situation with me alegra que, siento que and the subjunctive.
points.example: Me alegra que estés aquí.
points.example_en: I'm glad you're here.

points.name: subjunctive after doubt
points.can_do_en: Can express doubt with dudo que, no creo que and the subjunctive.
points.example: Dudo que llegue a tiempo.
points.example_en: I doubt he'll arrive on time.

points.name: subjunctive after impersonal expressions
points.can_do_en: Can use es importante que, es mejor que and es posible que with the subjunctive.
points.example: Es importante que estudies todos los días.
points.example_en: It's important that you study every day.

points.name: subjunctive after recommend, ask, suggest
points.can_do_en: Can recommend, ask and suggest with a verb plus que plus the subjunctive.
points.example: Te recomiendo que leas este libro.
points.example_en: I recommend that you read this book.

points.name: irregular subjunctive forms
points.can_do_en: Can use sea, esté, vaya, sepa, haya and dé in the subjunctive.
points.example: Ojalá que sepas la respuesta y que seas feliz.
points.example_en: I hope you know the answer and that you are happy.

points.name: subjunctive after cuando for the future
points.can_do_en: Can use cuando and the subjunctive for a future event that has not yet happened.
points.example: Cuando llegue a casa, te llamaré.
points.example_en: When I get home, I'll call you.

points.name: para que + subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can state a purpose that involves another person with para que.
points.example: Te explico esto para que lo entiendas.
points.example_en: I'm explaining this so that you understand it.

points.name: indicative vs subjunctive after creer
points.can_do_en: Can contrast creo que with the indicative and no creo que with the subjunctive.
points.example: Creo que viene, pero no creo que venga solo.
points.example_en: I think he's coming, but I don't think he'll come alone.

points.name: affirmative imperative with pronouns
points.can_do_en: Can attach pronouns to affirmative commands and write the accent.
points.example: Dímelo ahora y siéntate aquí.
points.example_en: Tell me now and sit down here.

points.name: negative imperative with pronouns
points.can_do_en: Can put pronouns before negative commands.
points.example: No me lo digas ni te lo lleves.
points.example_en: Don't tell me and don't take it away.

points.name: ustedes imperative
points.can_do_en: Can address a group politely with the ustedes imperative.
points.example: Pasen y siéntense, por favor.
points.example_en: Come in and have a seat, please.

points.name: double object pronouns
points.can_do_en: Can put the indirect pronoun before the direct pronoun, as in me lo and te la.
points.example: Mi mamá me lo dio ayer.
points.example_en: My mom gave it to me yesterday.

points.name: le/les becomes se before lo/la
points.can_do_en: Can change le or les to se before lo, la, los and las.
points.example: Se lo expliqué a mi jefe.
points.example_en: I explained it to my boss.

points.name: se me + unplanned events
points.can_do_en: Can say that something happened by accident with se me, se te and se le.
points.example: Se me cayó el vaso y se me olvidó el paraguas.
points.example_en: I dropped the glass and I forgot the umbrella.

points.name: passive se
points.can_do_en: Can use se with a verb to say what is done without naming who does it.
points.example: Aquí se habla español y se venden frutas.
points.example_en: Spanish is spoken here and fruit is sold.

points.name: impersonal se
points.can_do_en: Can use se with a singular verb for people in general.
points.example: En México se come mucho maíz. Se vive bien aquí.
points.example_en: In Mexico people eat a lot of corn. One lives well here.

points.name: ser + participle passive
points.can_do_en: Can read and use simple passives with ser and a participle that agrees.
points.example: La casa fue construida en 1990.
points.example_en: The house was built in 1990.

points.name: llevar + time + gerund
points.can_do_en: Can say how long I have been doing something with llevar and a gerund.
points.example: Llevo tres años estudiando español.
points.example_en: I've been studying Spanish for three years.

points.name: seguir + gerund
points.can_do_en: Can say that an action continues with seguir and a gerund.
points.example: Sigo trabajando en el mismo lugar.
points.example_en: I'm still working in the same place.

points.name: soler and volver a
points.can_do_en: Can say what I usually do with soler and what I do again with volver a.
points.example: Suelo caminar al trabajo y vuelvo a casa tarde.
points.example_en: I usually walk to work and I come back home late.

points.name: deber vs deber de
points.can_do_en: Can express obligation with deber and probability with deber de.
points.example: Debes dormir más. Debe de estar cansado.
points.example_en: You should sleep more. He must be tired.

points.name: mejor, peor, mayor, menor
points.can_do_en: Can use the irregular comparatives mejor, peor, mayor and menor.
points.example: Mi hermano es mayor que yo, pero mi hermana es menor.
points.example_en: My brother is older than me, but my sister is younger.

points.name: adjective position and apocope
points.can_do_en: Can choose the position of the adjective and shorten bueno, malo and grande.
points.example: Es un buen amigo y vive en una gran ciudad.
points.example_en: He's a good friend and lives in a great city.

points.name: relatives quien, donde, lo que
points.can_do_en: Can use quien, donde and lo que to join ideas.
points.example: La mujer con quien hablé es mi vecina.
points.example_en: The woman I spoke with is my neighbor.

points.name: lo + adjective
points.can_do_en: Can use lo with an adjective to talk about an idea in general.
points.example: Lo importante es descansar.
points.example_en: The important thing is to rest.

points.name: si + present (real conditions)
points.can_do_en: Can state a likely condition and its result with si and the present.
points.example: Si llueve, nos quedamos en casa.
points.example_en: If it rains, we stay home.

points.name: si + imperfect subjunctive (hypothetical)
points.can_do_en: Can talk about an unlikely or imaginary situation with si, the imperfect subjunctive and the conditional.
points.example: Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría más.
points.example_en: If I had time, I would travel more.

points.name: por vs para (cause, recipient, deadline)
points.can_do_en: Can contrast por for cause and exchange with para for recipient and deadline.
points.example: Lo hice por ti, pero es para mi mamá.
points.example_en: I did it for you, but it's for my mom.

points.name: verbs with fixed prepositions
points.can_do_en: Can use verbs with their usual preposition, such as pensar en and soñar con.
points.example: Pienso en ti. Sueño con viajar y dependo de mi familia.
points.example_en: I think about you. I dream of traveling and I depend on my family.

points.name: aunque + indicative
points.can_do_en: Can concede a fact with aunque and the indicative.
points.example: Aunque estoy cansado, sigo trabajando.
points.example_en: Although I'm tired, I keep working.

points.name: simple reported speech
points.can_do_en: Can report what someone said with dijo que and a past tense.
points.example: Ana dijo que estaba cansada.
points.example_en: Ana said she was tired.

points.name: indirect questions
points.can_do_en: Can embed a question after no sé, me preguntó or dime.
points.example: Me preguntó dónde vivía. No sé qué hora es.
points.example_en: He asked me where I lived. I don't know what time it is.

points.name: ¿verdad? and ¿no? tags
points.can_do_en: Can confirm information with tags such as ¿verdad? and ¿no? at the end of a sentence.
points.example: Vienes mañana, ¿verdad? Hace frío, ¿no?
points.example_en: You're coming tomorrow, right? It's cold, isn't it?

points.name: exclamations with qué and cuánto
points.can_do_en: Can react with ¡qué + adjective! and ¡cuánto / cuánta + noun! in everyday speech.
points.example: ¡Qué bonito! ¡Cuánta gente hay aquí!
points.example_en: How pretty! There are so many people here!

points.name: diminutives -ito and -ita
points.can_do_en: Can form and understand diminutives for size and affection.
points.example: Mi perrito es chiquito y vive en una casita.
points.example_en: My little dog is tiny and lives in a little house.

points.name: years and full dates
points.can_do_en: Can say years and full dates aloud and in writing.
points.example: Nací en 1995. Hoy es el 12 de octubre de 2024.
points.example_en: I was born in 1995. Today is October 12, 2024.

points.name: future perfect
points.can_do_en: Can say what will have happened by a future point with habré and a participle.
points.example: Para el viernes ya habré terminado el informe.
points.example_en: By Friday I'll have finished the report.

points.name: conditional perfect
points.can_do_en: Can say what would have happened with habría and a participle.
points.example: Yo no habría aceptado esa oferta.
points.example_en: I wouldn't have accepted that offer.

points.name: imperfect subjunctive forms
points.can_do_en: Can form the imperfect subjunctive and use it after past triggers.
points.example: Quería que me ayudaras con la mudanza.
points.example_en: I wanted you to help me with the move.

points.name: present perfect subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can use haya + participle for a completed event after a subjunctive trigger.
points.example: Me alegra que hayas llegado bien.
points.example_en: I'm glad you arrived safely.

points.name: pluperfect subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can use hubiera + participle for a wish about the past.
points.example: Ojalá hubiera estudiado más.
points.example_en: I wish I had studied more.

points.name: si + pluperfect subjunctive (third conditional)
points.can_do_en: Can talk about unreal past situations with si hubiera and habría.
points.example: Si hubiera sabido la verdad, habría actuado distinto.
points.example_en: If I had known the truth, I would have acted differently.

points.name: mixed conditionals
points.can_do_en: Can link an unreal past condition to a present result.
points.example: Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería doctora.
points.example_en: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.

points.name: como si + imperfect subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can compare with an imaginary situation using como si.
points.example: Habla como si lo supiera todo.
points.example_en: He talks as if he knew everything.

points.name: sequence of tenses in the subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can match present or imperfect subjunctive to the tense of the main verb.
points.example: Me pidió que le prestara dinero. Espero que me lo devuelva.
points.example_en: He asked me to lend him money. I hope he gives it back.

points.name: aunque + subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can use aunque with the subjunctive for a possible or irrelevant fact.
points.example: Aunque llueva, saldré a correr.
points.example_en: Even if it rains, I'll go for a run.

points.name: subjunctive in relative clauses (unknown)
points.can_do_en: Can describe a person or thing I may not find with que plus the subjunctive.
points.example: Busco a alguien que hable japonés.
points.example_en: I'm looking for someone who speaks Japanese.

points.name: subjunctive after nobody, nothing
points.can_do_en: Can say nobody or nothing exists with a relative clause in the subjunctive.
points.example: No hay nadie que sepa la respuesta.
points.example_en: There is nobody who knows the answer.

points.name: en cuanto, antes de que, hasta que
points.can_do_en: Can use time conjunctions with the subjunctive for future events.
points.example: En cuanto termine, te aviso. Antes de que te vayas, firma aquí.
points.example_en: As soon as I finish, I'll let you know. Before you go, sign here.

points.name: a menos que, con tal de que, sin que
points.can_do_en: Can use a menos que, con tal de que and sin que with the subjunctive.
points.example: Te lo presto con tal de que me lo devuelvas.
points.example_en: I'll lend it to you as long as you give it back.

points.name: quizás and tal vez with the subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can express possibility with quizás, tal vez and a lo mejor.
points.example: Quizás venga mañana. A lo mejor tiene razón.
points.example_en: Maybe he'll come tomorrow. Maybe he's right.

points.name: ojalá + imperfect subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can express a hard-to-reach wish with ojalá and the imperfect subjunctive.
points.example: Ojalá tuviera más tiempo libre.
points.example_en: I wish I had more free time.

points.name: ser passive with por
points.can_do_en: Can name the agent in a passive with ser, a participle and por.
points.example: La novela fue escrita por un autor chileno.
points.example_en: The novel was written by a Chilean author.

points.name: passive se vs ser passive
points.can_do_en: Can choose between se and ser + participle by register and focus.
points.example: Se aprobaron las leyes nuevas. Fueron aprobadas por el congreso.
points.example_en: The new laws were approved. They were approved by Congress.

points.name: estar + participle (resulting state)
points.can_do_en: Can describe a result with estar and an agreeing participle.
points.example: La puerta está cerrada y las cartas ya están enviadas.
points.example_en: The door is closed and the letters are already sent.

points.name: adjectives that change meaning
points.can_do_en: Can tell apart pairs such as ser aburrido and estar aburrido, ser listo and estar listo.
points.example: Mi jefe es listo, pero no está listo para la reunión.
points.example_en: My boss is clever, but he isn't ready for the meeting.

points.name: reported speech with tense backshift
points.can_do_en: Can shift tenses when reporting, for example present to imperfect and future to conditional.
points.example: Dijo que había terminado y que vendría mañana.
points.example_en: He said he had finished and would come tomorrow.

points.name: reporting requests and questions
points.can_do_en: Can report commands with pedir que and questions with preguntar si.
points.example: Me pidió que lo ayudara y preguntó si habíamos comido.
points.example_en: He asked me to help him and asked whether we had eaten.

points.name: time and place shifts in reporting
points.can_do_en: Can adjust words like hoy, aquí and mañana when reporting.
points.example: Dijo que lo haría al día siguiente y que allí hacía frío.
points.example_en: She said she would do it the next day and that it was cold there.

points.name: el cual and el que after prepositions
points.can_do_en: Can use el cual, la cual and el que after prepositions in longer sentences.
points.example: La razón por la cual renuncié es personal.
points.example_en: The reason why I resigned is personal.

points.name: cuyo, cuya, cuyos, cuyas
points.can_do_en: Can use cuyo to link a noun to its owner and make it agree with the thing owned.
points.example: El autor cuyo libro leí vive en Bogotá.
points.example_en: The author whose book I read lives in Bogotá.

points.name: lo que and lo cual
points.can_do_en: Can refer to a whole idea with lo que and lo cual.
points.example: No vino, lo cual me sorprendió. Lo que dices es cierto.
points.example_en: He didn't come, which surprised me. What you say is true.

points.name: adverbial gerund clauses
points.can_do_en: Can use a gerund to give a manner, cause or condition.
points.example: Saliendo temprano, llegarás a tiempo.
points.example_en: If you leave early, you'll arrive on time.

points.name: al + infinitive and sin + infinitive
points.can_do_en: Can express time with al plus infinitive and absence with sin plus infinitive.
points.example: Al llegar a casa, me cambié. Sin decir nada, se fue.
points.example_en: When I got home, I changed. Without saying anything, he left.

points.name: absolute participle clauses
points.can_do_en: Can open a sentence with a participle clause to show time or cause.
points.example: Terminado el trabajo, volvimos a casa.
points.example_en: With the work finished, we went back home.

points.name: pronoun placement with periphrases
points.can_do_en: Can place pronouns before or after the whole verb chain.
points.example: Te lo voy a decir. Voy a decírtelo.
points.example_en: I'm going to tell you. I'm going to tell you.

points.name: hacer + infinitive (causation)
points.can_do_en: Can say I cause something to be done with hacer plus an infinitive.
points.example: Hice reparar el carro. Me hizo reír.
points.example_en: I had the car repaired. He made me laugh.

points.name: por lo tanto, así que, de modo que
points.can_do_en: Can state a result with por lo tanto, así que and de modo que.
points.example: Llovía mucho; por lo tanto, cancelamos el paseo.
points.example_en: It was raining a lot; therefore, we cancelled the outing.

points.name: a pesar de, sin embargo, aun así
points.can_do_en: Can give a contrast with a pesar de, sin embargo and aun así.
points.example: A pesar de la lluvia, fuimos al parque.
points.example_en: Despite the rain, we went to the park.

points.name: conversation fillers and markers
points.can_do_en: Can use bueno, o sea, pues and la verdad to manage a conversation.
points.example: Bueno, o sea, la verdad es que no lo sé.
points.example_en: Well, I mean, the truth is that I don't know.

points.name: verbs with prepositional complements
points.can_do_en: Can use verbs such as enamorarse de, insistir en and casarse con.
points.example: Se enamoró de ella. Insiste en ir y se casó con él.
points.example_en: He fell in love with her. He insists on going and he married him.

points.name: fixed expressions with por and para
points.can_do_en: Can use estar por, por si acaso, para colmo and por lo menos.
points.example: Lo hice por si acaso. Por lo menos lo intenté.
points.example_en: I did it just in case. At least I tried.

points.name: double negatives
points.can_do_en: Can use no with nadie, nunca, nada and ningún in the same sentence.
points.example: No dije nada a nadie. Nunca he visto nada así.
points.example_en: I didn't say anything to anyone. I've never seen anything like it.

points.name: prefixes and suffixes
points.can_do_en: Can use des-, in-, re-, -dad and -ción to build and understand words.
points.example: Es imposible reinventar la rueda.
points.example_en: It's impossible to reinvent the wheel.

points.name: augmentatives -ón, -azo
points.can_do_en: Can recognise augmentatives such as -ón, -ote and -azo and their tone.
points.example: Vive en un casón enorme y siempre da un portazo al salir.
points.example_en: He lives in a huge house and always slams the door when he leaves.

points.name: fractions and percentages
points.can_do_en: Can say fractions, decimals and percentages aloud.
points.example: El veinticinco por ciento es un cuarto del total.
points.example_en: Twenty-five percent is a quarter of the total.

points.name: -ra and -se imperfect subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can recognise the -se forms and use -ra forms for polite wishes with quisiera.
points.example: Quisiera pedirle un favor. Si tuviese tiempo, lo haría yo.
points.example_en: I would like to ask you a favor. If I had time, I would do it myself.

points.name: por más que, por mucho que
points.can_do_en: Can concede with por más que and por mucho que plus the subjunctive.
points.example: Por más que lo intente, no lo logro.
points.example_en: No matter how hard I try, I can't do it.

points.name: reduplicated subjunctive (pase lo que pase)
points.can_do_en: Can use fixed patterns such as pase lo que pase and sea como sea.
points.example: Pase lo que pase, te apoyaré.
points.example_en: Whatever happens, I'll support you.

points.name: no es que + subjunctive
points.can_do_en: Can deny a possible reason with no es que and the subjunctive.
points.example: No es que no quiera ayudarte, es que no puedo.
points.example_en: It's not that I don't want to help you; it's that I can't.

points.name: aunque: indicative vs subjunctive nuance
points.can_do_en: Can show whether a fact is known or hypothetical by choosing the mood after aunque.
points.example: Aunque es caro, lo compro. Aunque fuera caro, lo compraría.
points.example_en: Although it's expensive, I'm buying it. Even if it were expensive, I'd buy it.

points.name: de + infinitive as a condition
points.can_do_en: Can replace a si clause with de plus an infinitive.
points.example: De haberlo sabido, habría venido antes.
points.example_en: Had I known, I would have come earlier.

points.name: en caso de que, siempre que, siempre y cuando
points.can_do_en: Can state a condition with en caso de que and siempre y cuando.
points.example: En caso de que llame, dile que no estoy.
points.example_en: In case he calls, tell him I'm not here.

points.name: conditional for past probability
points.can_do_en: Can guess about the past with the conditional.
points.example: Serían las tres cuando salimos.
points.example_en: It must have been three o'clock when we left.

points.name: formal se in notices and rules
points.can_do_en: Can read and write notices with se plus a verb, such as se prohíbe and se alquila.
points.example: Se prohíbe fumar. Se alquilan habitaciones.
points.example_en: Smoking is prohibited. Rooms for rent.

points.name: ser passive in news and formal texts
points.can_do_en: Can use the ser passive in formal text with agents and tenses.
points.example: Fue declarado ganador por el jurado.
points.example_en: He was declared the winner by the jury.

points.name: uno and se for generalising
points.can_do_en: Can generalise with uno, se dice and se cree.
points.example: Uno nunca sabe lo que va a pasar. Se dice que es rico.
points.example_en: You never know what will happen. They say he's rich.

points.name: third person plural impersonal
points.can_do_en: Can use the ellos form for unspecified people, as in dicen que and llaman.
points.example: Dicen que va a llover. Están llamando a la puerta.
points.example_en: They say it's going to rain. Someone is knocking at the door.

points.name: infinitive as a noun
points.can_do_en: Can use an infinitive as a subject or noun, with or without el.
points.example: Fumar es perjudicial. El saber no ocupa lugar.
points.example_en: Smoking is harmful. Knowledge takes up no space.

points.name: lo + adjective + de / lo que
points.can_do_en: Can build nominal phrases such as lo bueno de, lo mucho que and lo difícil que.
points.example: Lo bueno de vivir aquí es la tranquilidad.
points.example_en: The good thing about living here is the peace and quiet.

points.name: turning verbs and adjectives into nouns
points.can_do_en: Can build nouns with -ción, -miento, -eza and -dad.
points.example: La construcción del puente mostró la belleza del diseño.
points.example_en: The construction of the bridge showed the beauty of the design.

points.name: formal relatives (quienes, los cuales)
points.can_do_en: Can use quienes, los cuales and la mayoría de los cuales in formal writing.
points.example: Los estudiantes, la mayoría de los cuales viven lejos, llegan tarde.
points.example_en: The students, most of whom live far away, arrive late.

points.name: relative + preposition + article
points.can_do_en: Can use el que, el cual and donde after prepositions to link longer clauses.
points.example: El motivo por el que vine es claro.
points.example_en: The reason I came is clear.

points.name: por muy ... que
points.can_do_en: Can concede with por muy plus adjective plus que and the subjunctive.
points.example: Por muy difícil que sea, lo lograremos.
points.example_en: However hard it may be, we will manage.

points.name: siendo así, habiendo + participle
points.can_do_en: Can use the gerund, as in siendo así and habiendo terminado, to link ideas.
points.example: Habiendo terminado el trabajo, nos fuimos.
points.example_en: Having finished the work, we left.

points.name: echar a, ponerse a, llegar a
points.can_do_en: Can use aspect periphrases such as echar a correr, ponerse a and llegar a ser.
points.example: Se puso a llorar y luego echó a correr.
points.example_en: She started crying and then broke into a run.

points.name: deber de, haber de, tener que + haber
points.can_do_en: Can express probability and deduction with deber de, haber de and tener que.
points.example: Ha de ser difícil. Tiene que haberlo olvidado.
points.example_en: It must be hard. He must have forgotten it.

points.name: impersonal haber in all tenses
points.can_do_en: Can use hubo, había, habrá and haya correctly in impersonal sentences.
points.example: Hubo muchos problemas. Habrá que esperar.
points.example_en: There were many problems. We'll have to wait.

points.name: ser de, estar para, estar por
points.can_do_en: Can use phrases such as ser de, estar para and estar por.
points.example: El libro es de Ana. Estoy por irme.
points.example_en: The book is Ana's. I'm about to leave.

points.name: redundant clitics with a topic
points.can_do_en: Can repeat an object with a pronoun for emphasis, as in a Pedro le di el libro.
points.example: A Pedro le di el libro. Lo del dinero ya lo hablé.
points.example_en: I gave Pedro the book. I already talked about the money.

points.name: leísmo (recognition only)
points.can_do_en: Can recognise le used for a male direct object, which is common in Spain, without using it.
points.example: Lo vi ayer en la oficina.
points.example_en: I saw him yesterday at the office.

points.name: dative of interest (se me, se le)
points.can_do_en: Can interpret pronouns that show who is affected, as in se me durmió el niño.
points.example: Se me durmió el niño en el carro.
points.example_en: My child fell asleep on me in the car.

points.name: rich reporting verbs
points.can_do_en: Can report with verbs such as asegurar, admitir, negar and prometer.
points.example: Aseguró que no había visto nada y admitió haberse equivocado.
points.example_en: He claimed he hadn't seen anything and admitted he had been wrong.

points.name: formal connectors
points.can_do_en: Can structure writing with no obstante, en consecuencia and por consiguiente.
points.example: No obstante, los resultados fueron buenos y, en consecuencia, seguiremos.
points.example_en: However, the results were good and, as a result, we will go on.

points.name: hedging and stance
points.can_do_en: Can soften statements with parece que, cabe señalar que and en mi opinión.
points.example: Cabe señalar que, en mi opinión, el plan es viable.
points.example_en: It should be noted that, in my opinion, the plan is viable.

points.name: formal and informal register
points.can_do_en: Can write a formal opening and closing and adjust register to the reader.
points.example: Estimado señor Pérez: Le escribo para solicitar información.
points.example_en: Dear Mr. Pérez: I am writing to request information.

points.name: cleft sentences with ser
points.can_do_en: Can focus an element with lo que ... es and es ... donde.
points.example: Lo que más me gusta es viajar. Es en esta ciudad donde nací.
points.example_en: What I like most is traveling. It's in this city that I was born.

points.name: Spanish punctuation
points.can_do_en: Can use ¿ ?, ¡ !, the dash and angle quotes correctly.
points.example: ¿Qué dices? ¡No puede ser! Dijo: «Vamos».
points.example_en: What are you saying? It can't be! He said: "Let's go."

points.name: -ísimo and other intensifiers
points.can_do_en: Can intensify adjectives with -ísimo and with muy, sumamente and rete.
points.example: Es riquísimo y facilísimo de preparar.
points.example_en: It's extremely tasty and super easy to make.

points.name: stance adverbs
points.can_do_en: Can use efectivamente, precisamente and justamente to confirm or point out.
points.example: Efectivamente, eso es lo que dije.
points.example_en: Indeed, that is what I said.

points.name: cuanto más ... más, de lo que
points.can_do_en: Can express proportion with cuanto más ... más and compare with de lo que.
points.example: Cuanto más estudio, más aprendo.
points.example_en: The more I study, the more I learn.

points.name: fixed subjunctive phrases
points.can_do_en: Can use frozen forms such as que descanses, viva and sea como fuere.
points.example: ¡Que descanses! ¡Viva la libertad!
points.example_en: Sleep well! Long live freedom!

points.name: future subjunctive (recognition only)
points.can_do_en: Can recognise the future subjunctive in legal texts and proverbs without using it.
points.example: Adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres.
points.example_en: Wherever you go, do as you see.

points.name: si bien, aun si, y si
points.can_do_en: Can use si bien, aun si and y si for concession and doubt.
points.example: Si bien es cierto, aun si fuera falso, no cambiaría nada.
points.example_en: Although it is true, even if it were false, nothing would change.

points.name: imperfect of courtesy and narration
points.can_do_en: Can soften a request with the imperfect and use it for narrative effect.
points.example: Perdone, quería preguntarle algo.
points.example_en: Excuse me, I wanted to ask you something.

points.name: historic present
points.can_do_en: Can use the present to narrate past events vividly.
points.example: En 1492, Colón llega a América.
points.example_en: In 1492, Columbus arrives in America.

points.name: pretérito anterior (recognition only)
points.can_do_en: Can recognise the literary form hubo + participle after apenas and cuando.
points.example: Apenas hubo terminado, salió corriendo.
points.example_en: As soon as he had finished, he ran out.

points.name: conditional of rumour in news
points.can_do_en: Can report unconfirmed news with the conditional or conditional perfect.
points.example: Según el diario, el presidente habría renunciado.
points.example_en: According to the paper, the president would have resigned.

points.name: passive with estar siendo
points.can_do_en: Can read and use estar siendo + participle for a passive in progress.
points.example: El proyecto está siendo evaluado por expertos.
points.example_en: The project is being evaluated by experts.

points.name: stacked clitics in complex chains
points.can_do_en: Can handle two clitics with gerunds, infinitives and commands in one chain.
points.example: Estaba dándoselo cuando entró él.
points.example_en: I was giving it to him when he walked in.

points.name: laísmo and loísmo (recognition only)
points.can_do_en: Can recognise laísmo and loísmo in some regional texts without using them.
points.example: La vi ayer y le di el libro.
points.example_en: I saw her yesterday and gave her the book.

points.name: voseo (recognition only)
points.can_do_en: Can recognise voseo forms such as vos sabés from Argentina and Central America, while using tú.
points.example: Tú sabes mucho de música, ¿verdad?
points.example_en: You know a lot about music, don't you?

points.name: queísmo and dequeísmo
points.can_do_en: Can avoid dequeísmo and queísmo with verbs like creer que and darse cuenta de que.
points.example: Creo que viene. Me di cuenta de que era tarde.
points.example_en: I think he's coming. I realized it was late.

points.name: subject placement and focus
points.can_do_en: Can place the subject after the verb for focus or new information.
points.example: Llegó tarde Ana. Primero llegaron ellos.
points.example_en: Ana arrived late. They arrived first.

points.name: advanced discourse markers
points.can_do_en: Can use ahora bien, en todo caso and cabe preguntarse to steer an argument.
points.example: Ahora bien, cabe preguntarse si es posible.
points.example_en: Now then, one has to ask whether it is possible.

points.name: irony and understatement
points.can_do_en: Can use irony and understatement, such as no está nada mal, with the right tone.
points.example: No está nada mal para un principiante.
points.example_en: It's not bad at all for a beginner.

points.name: proverbs and idioms
points.can_do_en: Can understand and use common proverbs and idioms.
points.example: A caballo regalado no se le miran los dientes.
points.example_en: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

points.name: regional vocabulary variation
points.can_do_en: Can recognise regional words for the same thing across Latin America.
points.example: El autobús se llama «camión» en México y «guagua» en el Caribe.
points.example_en: The bus is called "camión" in Mexico and "guagua" in the Caribbean.

points.name: indirect politeness
points.can_do_en: Can make very polite requests with the pattern ¿le importaría que + imperfect subjunctive?, as in this example.
points.example: ¿Le importaría que cerrara la ventana?
points.example_en: Would you mind if I closed the window?

points.name: pseudo-cleft sentences
points.can_do_en: Can build lo que ... es que and quien ... fue sentences for emphasis.
points.example: Lo que quiero es que me escuches. Fue Ana quien llamó.
points.example_en: What I want is for you to listen to me. It was Ana who called.

points.name: a + noun with clitic doubling
points.can_do_en: Can double a fronted object with a clitic, as in a Juan lo conocí.
points.example: A Juan lo conocí en Quito.
points.example_en: I met Juan in Quito.

points.name: estar a punto de, andar + gerund, ir + gerund
points.can_do_en: Can use estar a punto de, andar and ir with a gerund for fine aspect.
points.example: Estuvo a punto de caerse. Anda buscando trabajo.
points.example_en: He was about to fall. He's looking for a job.

points.name: ser and estar in abstract constructions
points.can_do_en: Can use constructions such as es de esperar, está por hacer and es que.
points.example: Eso es de esperar. La cena está por hacer.
points.example_en: That is to be expected. Dinner is yet to be made.

points.name: impersonal haber with pronouns
points.can_do_en: Can use hubo que and clitics with impersonal haber, as in los hubo.
points.example: Hubo que esperar. Problemas, los hubo siempre.
points.example_en: We had to wait. There have always been problems.

points.name: gerund as modifier of the object
points.can_do_en: Can distinguish the gerund as manner and as description of an object.
points.example: Me vio llegando. Cayendo la noche, regresamos.
points.example_en: He saw me arriving. As night was falling, we went back.

points.name: appreciative suffixes (-illo, -ucho, -ote)
points.can_do_en: Can use appreciative suffixes to add shades of meaning such as scorn or affection.
points.example: Es un cuartucho, pero la casita es linda.
points.example_en: It's a shabby little room, but the little house is nice.

points.name: learned affixes and roots
points.can_do_en: Can analyse words built with Greek and Latin roots, as in inconmensurable.
points.example: Es una belleza inconmensurable.
points.example_en: It is an immeasurable beauty.

points.name: collocations and light verbs
points.can_do_en: Can use fixed combinations like hacer caso, dar lugar and tomar en cuenta.
points.example: Tomó en cuenta mis ideas e hizo caso a mi consejo.
points.example_en: He took my ideas into account and heeded my advice.

points.name: una vez + participle
points.can_do_en: Can use una vez + participle and similar formal frames for sequence.
points.example: Una vez dichas esas palabras, se marchó.
points.example_en: Once those words were said, he left.

points.name: apposition and parentheticals
points.can_do_en: Can use commas to insert appositions and parenthetical comments.
points.example: Lima, capital de Perú, es una ciudad enorme.
points.example_en: Lima, the capital of Peru, is a huge city.

points.name: Roman numerals and large figures
points.can_do_en: Can read Roman numerals, centuries and very large numbers.
points.example: Estamos en el siglo XXI, en el año dos mil veinticuatro.
points.example_en: We are in the 21st century, in the year two thousand twenty-four.
